- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Overestimates near the end of forecast horizon; reduce final 5–7 day predictions by 2–5% to align with observed mean reversion.
- When true price rises sharply (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts with exaggerated peak; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or 10% above current trend.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing short-term reversals; add 1–2 day lag correction for sudden drops or spikes in true data.
- Forecast mean is typically 3–5% below true mean; apply upward bias of 3–5% to overall forecast average.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 5–7 days show strong upward trend, reduce forecast momentum to prevent overshoot.
